label: Manual gold route - anogenital ulcer initial management
goal: Evaluate an anogenital ulcer and commit to an evidence-backed first management state in context.

steps.reason: Anchor the route on the presenting finding without assigning etiology.
Establish one of the two principal etiologic contrasts.
Organize enabling conditions, fault, consequences, and discriminators without duplicating management.
Establish the competing high-consequence cause and early-serology caveat.
Prioritize HSV and syphilis while retaining rare infectious and noninfectious alternatives.
Choose and interpret syphilis testing without false early exclusion.
Use direct lesion testing to replace morphology-only certainty.
Include the required host and prevention test without confusing it with ulcer etiology.
Commit to the first diagnostic bundle and residual uncertainty.
Classify same-day testing, limited testing, or escalation states that alter conduct.
Choose etiologic, syndromic, presumptive, or escalation management under the applicable protocol.
Act on serious, special-population, persistent, or noninfectious alternatives.
Define result revision, reassessment, failure, and referral loops.
Communicate prognosis, prevention, privacy, partner actions, and uncertainty.
Integrate D-E-T-C-S-P as a coherent bounded performance.
Collect evidence, then branch to transfer or targeted remediation.
